walkthroughs.body_html:
Contamination = radioactive atoms on or in you. They keep emitting until they decay — hard to remove.

Irradiation = radiation hits you from a source outside. Move away and it stops — you don't become radioactive.

Protection: shielding (lead, concrete), distance, and short exposure time.

On an activity-vs-time graph, read the starting activity A₀. The half-life is the time taken for activity to fall to A₀/2.

Check it again: from A₀/2 to A₀/4 should take the same time. That's the half-life test.

Carbon dating: a bone has ¼ of the C-14 of a fresh sample. That's 2 half-lives → about 11,400 years old.

1897 Thomson — plum pudding: a blob of positive charge with electrons stuck inside.

1909 Rutherford — fired alpha particles at gold foil. Most went through, but a few bounced back. So most of the atom is empty space with a tiny, dense, positive nucleus.

1913 Bohr — electrons can only sit in fixed shells at set energies. Later: protons and neutrons inside the nucleus.

mcqs.q: A nurse stands near a gamma source for 5 minutes, then leaves. This is an example of:
options: Contamination
Irradiation
Fission
Fusion

mcqs.q: What did the alpha scattering experiment show?
options: Electrons have negative charge
Atoms are mostly empty space with a tiny positive nucleus
Neutrons have no charge
Atoms cannot be split

mcqs.q: What did Rutherford's alpha-scattering experiment show about the atom?
options: Beta radiation is most ionising because it consists of fast electrons.
Most of the atom is empty space, with a tiny dense positive nucleus.
It showed that alpha particles can pass through any material because they are massless.
It showed that atoms are solid spheres of positive charge with electrons embedded inside.

mcqs.q: Which type of nuclear radiation is most ionising?
options: Beta radiation is most ionising because it consists of fast electrons.
Gamma is most ionising because it can travel furthest and pass through almost anything.
Charge was created by friction and pulled the balloon to the wall.
Alpha radiation — large, doubly charged particles cause the most ionisation per unit distance.

mcqs.q: When you rub a balloon and stick it to the wall, what has been transferred?
options: Charge was created by friction and pulled the balloon to the wall.
Protons jumped from the balloon to the wall, causing static cling.
It showed that alpha particles can pass through any material because they are massless.
Electrons have been transferred between the balloon and the cloth (not the wall).
